node.statement: If f: |K| -> M is a homeomorphism onto a compact space M, then |K| is compact. The open stars st(v), over all vertices v of K, form an open cover of |K|: a point lies in the open star of every vertex having positive barycentric coordinate in its unique open simplex. Compactness gives a finite subcover st(v_1),...,st(v_N). A vertex w belongs to st(v) exactly when w=v, because w is the relative interior of the zero-simplex {w}; hence every vertex of K is among v_1,...,v_N, so K has finitely many vertices.
